Subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing — Acme Enterprise

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Short follow-up that captures the pain, success criteria, and early procurement framing so your CFO/Procurement has something to react to.

Summary (from today's call)
- Pain: unpredictable p95 latency spikes during high-concurrency rerank flows; caching misses amplify cost during bursts.
- Current stack: mixed GCP-hosted CPU fallback endpoints + ad-hoc GPU workers; limited cross-region routing.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms for 512-token rerank windows; 25-25% reduction in per-token cost after caching/batching; predictable throughput during peak events.

Procurement framing (so Michael can start budgeting):
- Preliminary commercial guardrail: $150k — $350k TCV (year 1 baseline), flexible by scope and committed throughput.
- Term options: 12- or 24-month commitments; we can propose a short pilot (3-month, limited capacity) to accelerate approvals.
- SLA highlights: 99.9% uptime target, p95 latency SLO language included in one-pager; credits for severe breaches.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Tech deep-dive / PoC planning (Dylan) — 60-75 min (week of Mar 23).
2) One-page commercial summary for CFO (Dev) — deliver by Apr 10 to feed procurement.
3) Editable mutual action plan attached — please add procurement dates/stakeholders.

Attachments: acme_procurement_onepager.pdf (one-pager for procurement), mutual_action_plan_acme_v2.xlsx (editable MAP)

Could you confirm:
- Procurement contact(s) and best email for the CFO/Procurement lead?
- Whether Procurement prefers a pilot-first approach or a direct annual commitment?

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148
